result.title: Graph Coarsening Enables Escaping Local Optima in Compute-Constrained Nonconvex MAX-CUT
result.summary: Because its binary optimization landscape contains exponentially many local optima, MAX-CUT is highly sensitive to initialization. We study Particle Polynomial Relaxation (PPR), a moment-based nonconvex continuous reformulation possessing an advantageous optimization landscape. We warm-start PPR with Combinatorial Multigrid (CMG), a spectral graph-coarsening method that produces structure-aware initial solutions in near-linear time without training data. On \texttt{t2g20} ($n=400$), benchmark instance with known exact optimum, the combined CMG+PPR pipeline reaches $97.5\%$ of optimum on average and $98.4\%$ on the best run. An extended variant with discrete local-search refinement reaches the published optimum on all sixty Biq Mac instances evaluated by a recent neural branch-and-bound method. Using a sparse CSR representation, the same approach scales to G-set instances with up to $20{,}000$ vertices reducing memory requirements by up to $3333\times$ while maintaining a consistent improvement over the CMG warm start. Gains are largest on sparse weighted graphs; on dense graphs we complement the pipeline with spectral sparsification.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究计算受限下的非凸 MAX-CUT：用谱图粗化方法 CMG 为基于矩松弛的 PPR 连续重述提供结构感知的热启动解，并配合稀疏 CSR 表示、谱稀疏化与局部搜索，在若干基准上逼近最优解并大幅降低内存。
AI.relevance_reason: 图粗化本质是多尺度状态抽象、热启动对应状态初始化，其对非凸景观中逃离局部最优的讨论可能与 latent 推理状态的初始化、多尺度组织及低内存状态表示形成类比线索，但属较远领域，需人工核查。
